I farm the way I know best: I keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the most steady system for my place in Quzhou County, and I only keep a smaller piece in cotton because cotton takes more watching and more spraying. I am 60 years old and my household has only 2 people, so I will not spread myself too thin. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on it to protect wheat at key stages and to support maize and cotton when the season turns dry, but I still want a simple plan that matches my labor and experience. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen to secure tillers and grain filling, and keep fertilizer balanced so the crop does not lodge too easily. After wheat harvest, I will put maize right back on the same land because that rotation fits my fields and gives stable grain output. I will use hybrid maize because I care most about yield and uniform ears. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area and manage it more carefully with more pesticide applications, because if I plant too much cotton at my age it becomes hard to keep up with the field work. I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage and fits the equipment and labor I can organize. My goal this year is not to chase the highest possible output, but to keep the farm steady, manageable, and productive across all 15 mu.
